title: Doenjang Jjigae
subtitle: Fermented soybean paste stew with tofu and vegetables
excerpt: Doenjang jjigae is a robust, everyday Korean stew built on a base of fermented soybean paste and anchovy stock. Soft tofu, courgette, mushrooms, and spring onions simmer in the savoury broth. It is eaten with rice at almost every Korean family meal.
sourceNotes: Doenjang jjigae is one of Korea's oldest everyday dishes. Doenjang, the fermented soybean paste at its heart, has been made in Korea for over two thousand years. The stew in various forms appears throughout Korean culinary history and remains one of the most frequently cooked home dishes in the country today.

glossaryTerms.definition: A fermented Korean soybean paste with a strong, savoury flavour. It is similar to Japanese miso but coarser in texture and more pungent. It forms the base of many Korean soups and stews and is one of the most important ingredients in the Korean pantry.

A light, savoury Korean stock made by simmering dried anchovies and dried kelp in water. It forms the base of many Korean soups and stews. It can be made in 15 minutes and provides a subtle depth of flavour without being fishy.

content.text: Doenjang jjigae takes 30 minutes and serves 4. It is the sort of stew that appears on Korean tables every single day. The bold, earthy flavour comes entirely from
, which dissolves into the stock and seasons the whole pot.

. Simmer 10 dried anchovies and a 10cm piece of dried kelp in 1 litre of water for 10 minutes, then discard the solids. If you want a vegetarian version, use plain water or a light vegetable stock and leave out the anchovies. The doenjang will still carry the dish.
Make the anchovy stock: simmer the dried anchovies in 900ml of water for 10 minutes. Remove the anchovies and discard.
Bring the stock to a gentle boil. Add the doenjang a tablespoon at a time, stirring and tasting between additions. The broth should be deeply savoury but not salty.
Add the garlic, courgette, and mushrooms. Simmer for 8 minutes until the vegetables are tender.
Add the tofu cubes. Simmer gently for 3 minutes. Do not stir vigorously or the tofu will break apart.
Stir in the gochujang if using. Add the spring onions. Taste and adjust seasoning. Serve hot, ladled into bowls, alongside steamed rice.

items.cause: Too much doenjang was added at once
items.fix: Add doenjang one tablespoon at a time and taste as you go. You can always add more but cannot take it out. Adding more water or more tofu can help dilute excess salt.

items.symptom: Tofu has crumbled into tiny pieces
items.cause: The stew was stirred too vigorously after the tofu was added
items.fix: Once tofu is in the pot, stir gently by shaking the pan or using a spoon to push liquid over the top. Firm tofu holds better than silken in this dish.

items.cause: Stock was not rich enough or doenjang was not given time to dissolve
items.fix: Make sure the anchovies simmer for a full 10 minutes. Stir the doenjang into a little warm stock in a small bowl first to fully dissolve before adding it to the pot.

content.text: This stew is an everyday Korean meal. It appears at breakfast, lunch, and dinner. It is always served with rice. It is one of the most cooked dishes in Korean homes. The flavour is strong and comforting. It is cheap and quick to make.
